findings.recommendation: `Account` is a type of the public HTTP API: every existing client that reads `user_name` from the account endpoint gets a missing field after deploy (null/undefined, or a deserialization error for strict clients). Mark the change **BREAKING** in the proposal's release note with what clients must do (read `userName`), and give consumers a transition: e.g. emit both keys for a deprecation period (keep `user_name` alongside `userName`, or version the endpoint) before removing the old one. The release note line "Changed: Account JSON uses camelCase." is neither marked BREAKING nor says what users must do.
findings.title: Renamed public JSON field breaks existing API consumers without warning

findings.evidence: ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN legacy_email;
findings.recommendation: Running migration 0005 deletes every value still stored in `users.legacy_email` (the 2023 import data); the column is unwritten, not empty. Unlike `0004_accounts.down.sql`, there is no `0005_drop_legacy_email.down.sql`, and neither the proposal nor tasks.md plans a backup or explains how to recover. Add a down migration that re-creates the column (`ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN legacy_email TEXT;`), and a backup step (copy the column to an archive table or dump it) before the drop — or state in the plan why the data can be lost and how to recover it.
findings.title: DROP COLUMN is irreversible, with no down migration and no backup step

findings.evidence: ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN legacy_email;
findings.recommendation: No reader of `legacy_email` is visible in this repository, but the plan does not say that no running service, report or `SELECT *` consumer still reads it. If one does, it fails as soon as the migration runs during a rolling deploy. Confirm no consumer reads the column (or stop reading it in a release before the one that drops it — expand/contract), and note the rollout order in the plan.
findings.title: Column dropped in the same release as code, while old instances may still read it
